doc.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014

chapter: Joan Rivers Show and Woody Herman
title: Joining Woody Herman as lead trumpet; Thad Jones and Mel Lewis
summary: Shear took the Woody Herman lead chair as a rite of passage; he also played in Mel Lewis's band while Thad Jones had left for Europe.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: And you took an early detour from the studios to go with Woody Herman?

Yeah, that happened early on when I moved to Los Angeles, so I didn’t really — although I did do some studio work right away in L.A. I turned it down when they first called me. I’ll never forget it. It was in the evening and I had to play a gig. So during the gig I was saying I should take that Woody Herman thing. Not that I needed to move out of town but I think it’s a big deal because they called me to play first trumpet, lead trumpet, and the lineage of lead trumpet players that Woody’s had through the years is just extraordinary, and to be a part of that list. And back then it was sort of a rite of passage. If you had that on your resume people would sort of — oh wow — I’ve had this come up in the studios and it was a big deal. If I got a call to play second or the third with Woody I probably wouldn’t have done it. Not to be an elitist or anything — and believe me I’m not — but it’s a very important chair to play. So I took it and I did it for a couple of years.
Boy, when I was here, that kind of thing, the jazz guys, that was a goal. There wasn’t that many big bands left but boy we just, oh God, if we could go with Buddy Rich.
You know, Stan Kenton came here and we just like thought that’s what we want to do.

Exactly. Yeah, and the big big band I always wanted to play with was Woody. Thad Jones too, which I ended up playing with in New York when I got out of Eastman — I lived with my folks in New York for one more year to study trumpet, and then I moved to L.A. and that year I was on — well it was mostly Mel’s band, at that point Mel Lewis’ band. Thad was already in Sweden or somewhere living. So that was the other great band I wanted to play with.
Do you happen to know why he just picked up and left?

Thad? I guess he had it from New York all those years. Maybe he wanted to live an easier life. And In Europe they have all these radio orchestras so you could get your music played every day and there’s a lot of opportunity. They love jazz there, much more than I think the United States, although Thad did live in New York, which is the thriving city for jazz I think in this country, still.
